slides.heading: Find Loop
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Find Loop, a hard linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: The list contains a cycle; return the node where the loop begins (Floyd's algorithm).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. The list contains a cycle; return the node where the loop begins (Floyd's algorithm).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Floyd's cycle detection: after slow and fast meet, a pointer from the head and one from the meeting point meet at the loop start.
slides.narration: Floyd's cycle detection: after slow and fast meet, a pointer from the head and one from the meeting point meet at the loop start.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Hash set of visited nodes → O(n) space
Floyd's tortoise and hare → O(1) space
Second phase finds the loop start
slides.narration: Storing visited nodes finds the loop start but uses memory. Floyd's algorithm uses two speeds to meet inside the loop, then a reset finds the start with constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 4. Move both by one until they meet
slides.narration: Step by step. First, slow moves one, fast two. Second, they meet inside the loop. Third, reset one to the head. Fourth, move both by one until they meet.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Loop back to node 4; slow 1 step, fast 2
slides.narration: The tail points back to node four. Slow moves one step, fast two.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: They meet at 6
slides.narration: They meet inside the loop, at node 6.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reset slow to head; both move 1 step
slides.narration: Reset slow to the head; now both move one step at a time.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Meet again at 4: loop start
slides.narration: After 4 steps they meet at node 4, the start of the loop. The distance from head to loop start equals the distance from the meeting point to loop start.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Slow and fast start one and two steps in and move until equal. Then slow restarts at the head and both move one step until they meet at the loop start.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Input always has a loop here
slides.narration: Initialise the pointers carefully and compare nodes by identity.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Be ready to prove why the reset works.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Floyd's cycle detection: after slow and fast meet, a pointer from the head and one from the meeting point meet at the loop start.
slides.narration: To recap Find Loop: Floyd's cycle detection: after slow and fast meet, a pointer from the head and one from the meeting point meet at the loop start. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
